title: Over 150,000 Flights: Airlines Just Flew The Busiest Day In Recorded History
excerpt: Late July is always a busy time for the commercial aviation sector.
content_html:
Published Jul 27, 2026, 4:18 AM EDT

A graduate in German, Jake has a passion for history and regional aviation, and enjoys sampling new carriers and aircraft. He has visited OEM facilities as far and wide as Bristol, Toulouse, and Seattle, and recently enjoyed the milestone of flying his 150th sector as a passenger. Based in Norfolk, UK.

Last week was a busy one in the world of aviation for several reasons. Airshow enthusiasts descended on events such as Farnborough and Oshkosh in their thousands, while Qantas and Airbus made history with a record-breaking nonstop A350-1000ULR test flight from Toulouse to Melbourne. However, on a wider level, the airline industry as a whole also made headlines with a record-setting day.

Indeed, Thursday, July 23, 2026 was the busiest-ever day for the commercial airline sector since records began in terms of flights operated, with more than 150,000 being tracked on that day alone. When aspects such as general, military, and private aviation were factored in, the total climbed to almost 300,000, making it the second-busiest day ever for aviation as a whole. Let's crunch the numbers!

A Day For The History Books

According to a statement released on social media yesterday by popular flight tracking website Flightradar24, a whopping grand total of 153,359 commercial flights were tracked between 00:00 UTC and 23:59 UTC on July 23, 2026. This is the most that the site has ever tracked in a single day, with the huge numbers being indicative of the summer travel rush that typically occurs in mid to late-July each year.

According to Newsweek, analysts say that leisure travel peaks in the Northern Hemisphere summer are driving this strong demand, despite aviation as a whole facing external challenges such as fuel price spikes tied to the Iran War. This time of year is always a busy one, with the CAA noting that UK airports and flights were expected to be at their busiest on July 24. Flightradar24 said on X that:

"The last week in July is often the busiest week for air travel, and this year is no exception. On Thursday we tracked 153,359 commercial flights: the most we’ve ever tracked."

The Most-Tracked Flight On The Busiest Day Was An Obvious One

With well over 150,000 commercial flights being tracked on July 23, most will likely have drawn little attention from avgeeks on flight tracking sites. However, there was one notable exception to this trend last Thursday, with the most-tracked flight of the day consistently being Airbus and Qantas' nonstop test flight from Toulouse Blagnac (TLS) to Melbourne Airport (MEL) using the Airbus A350-1000ULR.

In the 19 hours and 13 minutes that the ultra-long-range European widebody twinjet was in the air on its nonstop odyssey from France to Australia, the aircraft, which aptly bears the registration F-WULR, typically had around 9,000 users tracking it at any given time. Data from Flightradar24 shows that it left Toulouse at 7:33 AM on Thursday, July 23, and touched down in Melbourne at 10:46 AM the next day.

The site's most-tracked flight at the time of writing this article is the return leg of this test flight, which is also flying back from Melbourne to Toulouse on a nonstop basis. 40 minutes after takeoff, it had some 8,500 users tracking it as it flew northeast from Melbourne in the early stages of its return flight. Based on this trajectory, it looks set to fly across the Pacific, North America, and the Atlantic on its way home.

Busy Airshow Traffic Contributed To An Overall Total Of Almost 300,000

Of course, flight tracking tools such as Simple Flying's Flight Tracker don't just show avgeeks where commercial aircraft are flying. Indeed, users can also expect to be able to see general, military, and private aviation aircraft. When such flights are factored in, Flightradar24 tracked a combined total of 287,364 services on Thursday, July 23, 2026. Airshow traffic at Farnborough and Oshkosh was likely a factor.

This figure represented its second-busiest day ever in terms of total flights tracked. According to the site, it first topped the 200,000 mark back on June 29, 2025, and it repeated the feat on July 12 and 13 of that year. Flightradar24 says that its traffic typically peaks at the end of August, so we may yet see the record broken this year. Contrastingly, on Christmas Day (December 25), it barely tracks 100,000 flights.

content_html_zh:
发布于 2026 年 7 月 27 日凌晨 4:18（美国东部时间）

杰克毕业于德语，对历史和支线航空充满热情，并喜欢尝试新的航母和飞机。 他参观过远至布里斯托尔、图卢兹和西雅图的 OEM 工厂，最近还享受了作为乘客飞行第 150 个航段的里程碑。 总部位于英国诺福克。

由于多种原因，上周对于航空界来说是忙碌的一周。 数千名航展爱好者涌入范堡罗和奥什科什等航展，而澳洲航空和空客则通过从图卢兹飞往墨尔本的破纪录的不间断 A350-1000ULR 试飞创造了历史。 然而，从更广泛的层面来看，整个航空业也因创纪录的一天而成为头条新闻。

事实上，2026 年 7 月 23 日星期四是商业航空业自有航班运营记录以来最繁忙的一天，仅当天就有超过 150,000 架次的航班被追踪。 如果将通用航空、军用航空和私人航空等因素考虑在内，总数攀升至近 30 万架次，成为航空业有史以来第二繁忙的一天。 让我们来计算一下数字吧！

历史书籍的一天

根据热门航班跟踪网站 Flightradar24 昨天在社交媒体上发布的一份声明，在 2026 年 7 月 23 日 00:00 UTC 至 23:59 UTC 期间，追踪到的商业航班总数高达 153,359 架次。 这是该网站单日追踪的最高数字，这一巨大数字表明通常发生在每年 7 月中下旬的夏季旅游高峰。

据《新闻周刊》报道，分析师表示，尽管整个航空业面临伊朗战争导致的燃油价格飙升等外部挑战，但北半球夏季的休闲旅游高峰推动了这一强劲需求。 每年的这个时候总是繁忙的时候，英国民航局指出，预计 7 月 24 日英国机场和航班将达到最繁忙状态。 Flightradar24 在 X 上表示：

“七月的最后一周通常是航空旅行最繁忙的一周，今年也不例外。 周四，我们追踪到了 153,359 架次商业航班：这是我们追踪到的最多航班。”

最繁忙的一天中追踪次数最多的航班是显而易见的

7 月 23 日，有超过 150,000 架商业航班被追踪，大多数航班很可能不会引起航班追踪网站上的普通人的关注。 然而，上周四这一趋势有一个明显的例外，当天最受关注的航班始终是空客和澳洲航空使用空客 A350-1000ULR 从图卢兹布拉尼亚克 (TLS) 飞往墨尔本机场 (MEL) 的直达试飞。

这架超远程欧洲宽体双发喷气式飞机从法国到澳大利亚不间断飞行，在空中飞行了 19 小时 13 分钟，这架注册号为 F-WULR 的飞机在任何特定时间通常都会有约 9,000 名用户跟踪它。 Flightradar24的数据显示，该航班于7月23日星期四上午7点33分离开图卢兹，并于次日上午10点46分抵达墨尔本。

在撰写本文时，该网站追踪最多的航班是这次试飞的返程航班，该航班也是从墨尔本直飞图卢兹的航班。 起飞 40 分钟后，在返程初期从墨尔本向东北方向飞行时，大约有 8,500 名用户跟踪了它。 根据这个轨迹，它看起来将在回家途中飞越太平洋、北美和大西洋。

繁忙的航展客流量总计近30万人次

当然，诸如 Simple Flying 的 Flight Tracker 之类的航班跟踪工具不仅仅向普通爱好者展示商用飞机的飞行地点。 事实上，用户还可以期望能够看到通用、军用和私人航空飞机。 如果将此类航班考虑在内，Flightradar24 在 2026 年 7 月 23 日星期四总共追踪了 287,364 次服务。 范堡罗和奥什科什的航展交通可能是一个因素。

就跟踪的航班总数而言，这一数字是有史以来第二繁忙的一天。 据该网站称，它于 2025 年 6 月 29 日首次突破 20 万大关，并于当年 7 月 12 日和 13 日重复了这一壮举。 Flightradar24 表示，其流量通常在 8 月底达到峰值，因此今年我们可能会看到这一记录被打破。 相比之下，在圣诞节（12 月 25 日），它只追踪到 10 万个航班。
